struck: A conventional loan sold to Fannie Mae cannot close in a condo building whose association is a party to a pending lawsuit.
use: Fannie Mae will not buy a loan on a unit in a building whose association is named in a pending lawsuit, or whose developer is in a suit about the building's safety, structure, livability or use, unless the lender finds the suit minor in a way the guide lists.

struck: The building stays eligible if the suit is to recover money for repairs already made.
use: The building can stay eligible if the association is suing to recover money for repairs already made, and losing would not hurt it.

struck: A building that just settled can still fail FHA for a year.
use: For an FHA loan on one unit, a suit about the building's safety, structure, livability or use still counts for 12 months after it ends.

struck: The county's court index shows every suit against an association.
use: We search the county's court index under the association's name; a suit in federal court is listed elsewhere.

struck: Some judgments can be opened as images from the index.
use: (cut it: no one opened a court image from the index)

struck: A defect suit must be brought no later than eight years after the building was substantially completed.
use: For a building finished after mid-2005, a defect suit must be brought within three years of discovery and no later than eight years after completion; older buildings had 13 years.

use: Most condos for sale here are in buildings past the usual time limit for a builder suit, but a suit claiming gross negligence can still come years later, as Wedgewood's did.

use: Of the 2,860 condos for sale in the local MLS on the day we counted, 73 were in buildings built in 2018 or later.

use: The association sued in 2018, about 17 years after it was built, and the jury found gross negligence, which lifts the time limit.
